first.rationale: The competitor's aggressive entry pricing is the most acute, time-sensitive threat to SMB revenue retention, and memory_73 directly claims promotional pricing works for price-sensitive SMBs with acquisition, revenue, and time-to-value gains. Given only one experiment slot this week, addressing the competitive pricing pressure has the clearest link to the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. However, the archived summary doesn't address margin compression, long-term retention of discount-acquired accounts, or whether repeated discounting trains customers to expect lower prices — all relevant risks to 'sustainable' revenue that the memory record may not have tested for. I'm verifying memory_73's original record before committing since it underlies the costliest and most consequential lever (pricing directly affects margin structure and could interact badly with the competitor's pricing war). I'm not spending my second verification slot because the other two concerns (activation and onboarding decline) are smaller magnitude (6% and 4%) and don't require this week's single experiment slot — they can be queued for future cycles. Given the uncertainty around downstream margin/retention effects of discounting under competitive pressure, I recommend a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout, so we can observe cohort quality and retention signals before scaling exposure to a real price war dynamic.
